name: Smith & Nephew plc
executive_summary: Smith & Nephew is a global medtech group (Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT, Advanced Wound Management) that the quantitative screen rates **Strong Buy**, passing all five metric families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) on P/E ~19.4, P/B ~2.3, yield ~2.7%, ROE ~11.9% and debt/equity ~73%. The value case rests on a multi-year earnings and FCF recovery, active capital return ($500m buyback completed in 2025; a further $500m announced May 2026; a $250m tranche reported completed Aug 2026), and portfolio mix shifting toward higher-growth Sports Medicine. The central debate is whether H2 2026 product launches, skin-substitute stabilisation and US knee recovery can deliver management’s ~6% underlying revenue growth and ~$1.3bn trading profit guidance after Q2 underlying growth of 1.6% disappointed and the stock touched a 52-week low. Primary filing coverage in this pack is thin — one usable trading update, no indexed annual report or half-year results — so conviction is **partially confirmed**, not fully validated.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s Strong Buy signal aligns with a **quality medtech franchise trading at modest multiples** while fundamentals improve. Eight of 22 models pass, including Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value, Earnings Quality and Financial Health, with composite score 75% and persistent signal over nine weeks. Timing is neutral (RSI ~38, price ~12% below the 200-day moving average), which suits phased accumulation rather than momentum chasing.

Business quality is improving structurally. The Q1 2026 RNS reports Sports Medicine has overtaken Orthopaedic Reconstruction; innovation launched in the last five years drove more than half of growth; and the RISE strategy targets ~6% underlying revenue growth, ~$800m FCF and >10% adjusted ROIC in 2026. Yahoo annual data (no indexed annual report available — see Financial Review) shows revenue rising from $5.5bn (2023) to $6.2bn (2025), net income from $263m to $625m, and FCF from $181m to **$852m** — supporting the screen’s FCF and earnings-quality passes. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly: ~$330m dividends plus ~$502m repurchases in 2025, with management committing to return >$835m (buyback plus ordinary dividend) over the next twelve months per the Q1 trading update.

For a value investor, the overlay is a **recovering cash generator at ~20x earnings with a 2.7% yield and ongoing buybacks**, plus Cevian Capital building a ~14.21% stake (Aug 2026 news) as a governance catalyst the screen does not capture. The offset is near-term operational softness in US knees and wound bioactives, and CFO John Rogers’ departure (Aug 2026), which raises execution risk during a product-heavy H2.
financial_review:
**Primary filings — indexed coverage**

The `filings_index.json` catalogue lists 11 items: one trading update, one item mislabelled “annual” (CATALYSTEM 510(k) product release, Jul 2024), one mislabelled “interim” (TESSA FDA De Novo, Jul 2026), seven other product/regulatory/corporate items, and one legacy Companies House form (2007). **No annual report, 20-F/10-K, half-year results or Q2/H1 2026 RNS bodies are indexed.** Annual balance-sheet and income-statement trends below therefore fall back to Yahoo `financials_annual.json`, stated explicitly. Interim colour is limited to the Q1 2026 trading update; Q2/H1 detail is visible only via news headlines, not filing bodies.

**Q1 2026 trading update (primary — RNS body, 6 May 2026)**

- Revenue **$1,501m** (2025: $1,407m); underlying growth **+3.1%** (+4.7% on adjusted daily sales); reported **+6.6%** (350bps FX tailwind).
- Segments (underlying): Sports Medicine & ENT **+6.7%** ($491m); Advanced Wound Management **+2.2%** ($411m); Orthopaedics **+0.8%** ($599m), with US Knee Implants **−10.3%**.
- FY2026 guidance **unchanged**: ~**6%** underlying revenue growth; ~**$1.3bn** trading profit (including Integrity Orthopaedics); ~**$800m** FCF; >**10%** adjusted ROIC (excluding Integrity).
- Disclosed headwinds: ~**$60m** tariff impact; **$20–40m** incremental skin-substitute reimbursement reset; Integrity acquisition marginally dilutive to trading profit in 2026.
- Capital allocation: new **$500m** share buyback (follows $500m completed in 2025); financed from FCF and cash. Management cites a strong balance sheet and H2-weighted phasing for revenue and profit.

**Annual trends (fallback — Yahoo `financials_annual.json`; USD)**

Revenue and normalised earnings have recovered clearly from the 2023 trough. FCF conversion improved materially in 2024–25, aided by working-capital release in 2025 (inventory −$208m per cash-flow statement). Restructuring/M&A charges persisted ($62m in 2025; $184m in 2024) but the normalised trend is upward. Leverage is moderate: net debt ~$2.55bn against equity ~$5.29bn; interest expense $179m versus operating income $857m. Goodwill and intangibles of **$3.99bn** versus tangible book **$1.30bn** is typical for medtech but limits tangible-asset support for the P/B screen pass.

**Interim gap**

No indexed H1 2026 or FY2025 annual report bodies. The Q1 RNS calendar indicated H1/Q2 results on 4 Aug 2026, but that release is **not present** in the filing index. Q2 performance is visible only via news: “Smith & Nephew SNATS Q2 Earnings Call Highlights” (9 Aug 2026) reports underlying revenue growth of **1.6%**, below management expectations, with US Orthopaedics and Advanced Wound Bioactives offsetting strength in Sports Medicine and ENT. **Verify full H1 2026 results and FY2025 annual report before sizing positions.**
risks_and_flags:
**Operational / competitive:** US Knee Implants declined 10.3% in Q1 (management describes deliberate set-placement discipline ahead of the LANDMARK launch); Q2 group underlying growth of 1.6% (news only — no filing body) suggests the recovery trajectory is not yet evident. Orthopaedics faces intense competition from Stryker, Zimmer Biomet and others in robotics and cementless implants.

**Regulatory / reimbursement:** Skin-substitute reimbursement reset ($20–40m guided impact in Q1 RNS); China Volume-Based Procurement delayed to H2 2026 (ENT inventory reduction in Q1). Tariffs ~$60m. Active FDA pipeline (TESSA De Novo, CORI XT) does not guarantee uptake or payer coverage — filing forward-looking language explicitly flags reimbursement decisions and regulatory actions as material risks.

**Governance / key person:** CFO John Rogers resigned for an external role (Aug 2026; “Baxter hires CFO from Smith & Nephew”, 20 Aug 2026). Cevian Capital stake ~14.21% (Aug 2026) increases pressure for operational improvement. Orthopaedics president change (Nathan Folkert replacing Craig Gaffin, per Q1 RNS).

**Balance sheet / pension:** Net debt ~$2.55bn (Yahoo fallback); non-current pension and post-retirement obligations **$84m** (2025 balance sheet). No going-concern, covenant or contingency language appears in indexed filing bodies — those disclosures would sit in the missing annual/interim accounts.

**Source risk:** Thin primary coverage; do not treat Yahoo and a single trading update as a complete audit trail.

research_rationale: Deep research partially confirms the Strong Buy screen — improving FCF, reasonable multiples and active capital return support the case, but missing annual/interim filings, Q2 operational softness and CFO turnover mean verify-before-trade on full-year accounts and H1 results is essential.

meta_reflection.observation: Filings-first order is adequate only if period tags are true. For SN.L they are not: period_coverage annual=1/interim=1/trading_update=1 counts a Jul 2024 CATALYSTEM 510(k) as annual and a Jul 2026 TESSA FDA De Novo as interim, while the sole real operating RNS (Q1 2026 TU, 6 May) sits below empty yahoo_quarterly_cashflow on the ladder. No FY results, 20-F, or H1/Q2 2026 body is indexed despite news of an 5 Aug Q2 call. alternate_news and ir_presentation_metrics are absent; Yahoo quarterlies empty is expected for a USD half-year reporter, not equivalent to a missing statutory pack. Axis Bank “Listing/Allotment of SN” rows show ticker-collision ingest beating the ladder.

The screen emits strong_buy (8/22, five families, conviction 0.93, 9w persistent) on P/E 19.4 / FCF 1,059m while Yahoo FY FCF is 852m, operating income is flat, TTM cashflow is suppressed, and every healthcare/reimbursement/cash-conversion/interim overlay is false. Prior-loop research text is already spliced into action_note/summary (repeated Accumulate/partially-confirms boilerplate), so the director–worker trial is asked to re-verify a Strong Buy whose snapshot has been contaminated by an earlier memo that already admitted missing annual/interim filings. Qualitative veto is doing the work sector overlays failed to do.

Mandatory annual+interim summarize_filing_body plus news+screen+gap consumes the five-task cap on two product RNSs that are not results. There is no type or period flag for trading_update, 20-F, rns_cluster (PDMR/buyback/TVR), or “catalog_period_mismatch”. gap_inventory can only list that the Q1 TU — the only indexed financial body — and the unpublished H1 RNS were dropped. Workers cannot be told to treat a 510(k) as FY2025.

weeks_at_signal=9 / stable / conviction 0.93 looks like a settled Strong Buy, but there is no watch schema for: ingest of the Aug 2026 H1/Q2 RNS (news-visible, catalog-absent), FY2026 guidance vs Q2 1.6%, US knee / skin-substitute run-rate, CFO successor and Cevian 14.21%, remaining buyback vs £1,039/£997 ladder, ADS 52-week low vs LSE print, or post-4 Sep RNS. RSI 38 + SMA200-flat timing=neutral is not a substitute. News freshness reaches 4 Sep; filings_index fetched 17:25Z the same day still lacks the August results body — a same-day coverage hole, not a stale-data hole.

A generic FINANCIAL REVIEW / RISKS split will blend Yahoo USD statutory with company trading-profit/FCF and will not force Orthopaedics vs Sports Med & ENT vs Advanced Wound Management, US knees vs rest-of-world, skin-substitute reimbursement, FCF 1,059m vs 852m, ADS vs LSE price, or an explicit PRIMARY-FILING GAP box. Without SEGMENT MIX, REIMBURSEMENT, CAPITAL RETURNS, GUIDANCE PATH (Q1 TU → missing H1 → news Q2), and GOVERNANCE/ACTIVIST slots, workers will treat Kalkine SEO and SharkNinja/Chilean .SN collisions as colour. Director catalog pass can form these questions without drafting the memo.
